key_insight: A machine learning-guided SCAPS-1D workflow identified an optimized CdSnP2-based solar-cell/photodetector stack that substantially improves both power conversion and photodetection performance.
engineering_relevance: The study shows how data-driven layer and interface tuning can accelerate practical design of multifunctional optoelectronic devices with higher efficiency, responsivity, and detectivity.
method: SCAPS-1D generated device data by varying layer thickness, doping, and defect density.
Six machine learning models plus one deep learning model were trained and compared using an ensemble-based evaluation.
SHAP was used to explain which physical factors most influenced device performance.
evidence_signal: Across 13 candidate structures, the best design was n-CdS/p-CdSnP2/p+-CGS, with efficiency rising from 20.67% to 32.69%, responsivity from 0.53 to 0.72 A/W, and detectivity from 2.51×10^14 to 1.78×10^16 Jones.
watch_item: The optimization is simulation-driven, so experimental fabrication tolerance, interface quality, and real defect distributions may limit direct transfer to hardware.
paper_title: Machine learning-assisted design and explainable optimization of CdSnP2-based integrated solar-photodetector devices
